title: Topic 2 – Business combinations
source: Zusammenfassung von „IFRS Topic 2 fall 2026 student version“

blocks.text: Individual financial statements are prepared for each legal entity (generally in local GAAP); consolidated statements present the group as one economic entity. Consolidated statements matter because individual statements can hide the group's real leverage (example: individual debt/equity of 1 each, consolidated 7).

children: 1) Determine the scope of consolidation and the method for each entity
2) Prepare individual statements for consolidation: convert to IFRS, apply uniform accounting policies (IFRS 10.19), convert currencies

blocks.text: Scope and methods by type of relationship:
children: Passive investment (<20%): financial asset under IFRS 9
Joint control: joint venture (equity method) or joint operation (proportionate method), IFRS 11
Percentages are indicators – control is what counts
a) Purchase price allocation: allocate fair value–book value differences to identifiable assets/liabilities; the remainder is goodwill
b) Integrate 100% of the subsidiary's assets, liabilities, income and expenses, even below 100% ownership
c) Eliminate the investment in the subsidiary against its (acquisition-date) equity and eliminate intra-group transactions

blocks.text: Goodwill = purchase price − fair value of the identifiable net assets acquired. It reflects synergies, workforce and other non-identifiable elements. Positive goodwill is an intangible asset, not amortised but tested for impairment annually; negative goodwill is an immediate gain.
Valuation differences follow the asset they belong to (depreciation, impairment test). Impairments of brands can be reversed up to their original value; goodwill impairments never.

Non-controlling interest is the minority shareholders' share in a subsidiary's equity and net income; it is presented separately within consolidated equity, and consolidated net income is split into group share and NCI share.

Equity method: the investment follows the associate's equity (cost + share of profits − dividends), shown in one line in the balance sheet and one line in the income statement; PPA still applies; no NCI.
Critical issues for analysts: scope of consolidation and its changes (pro forma information), goodwill (PPA, impairment test), related-party transactions.
An entity controlled by another entity (the parent).
An entity over which the investor has significant influence (presumed from 20% of voting rights).
Allocation of the purchase price to the identifiable assets and liabilities of the acquiree at fair value; the remainder is goodwill.
The excess of the purchase price over the fair value of the identifiable net assets acquired.
Equity in a subsidiary not attributable, directly or indirectly, to the parent.

Exam recipe (consolidated BS at acquisition): 1) equity of the subsidiary at book value, 2) + fair value adjustments, 3) goodwill = price − fair value of net assets, 4) add all assets/liabilities line by line with fair value adjustments, add goodwill, remove the investment, 5) equity = parent's equity (+ NCI). Check: total assets = total equity & liabilities.
